policies.title: Irish citizens: citizenship entry status
policies.summary: An Irish ordinary passport represents citizenship rather than a short-stay visitor-visa route.
conditions: This policy records citizenship, not a visa exemption or border permission for a non-national.
It does not determine the treatment of a different passport used by a dual Irish citizen.

policies.title: EU citizens: free-movement entry
policies.summary: The listed EU citizens do not need an Irish visa or other special permission for ordinary travel to Ireland; their entry is governed by free-movement rules rather than a visitor-visa waiver.
conditions: Applies to a citizen of the named EU state using a valid national identity card or passport as evidence of nationality and identity.
The statutory entry rule preserves public-health, public-policy and public-security exceptions; it is not an unconditional admission guarantee.
This policy does not cover citizens of EU overseas territories or possessions that Ireland says do not qualify for single-market free movement.

policies.title: EEA and Swiss citizens: free-movement entry
policies.summary: Icelandic, Liechtenstein, Norwegian and Swiss citizens do not need an Irish visa or other special permission for ordinary travel to Ireland under the single-market/free-movement framework.
conditions: Applies to citizens of the named state; Switzerland is not in the EEA but Ireland identifies its agreement extending the single market.
Entry remains subject to the identity-document and individual public-health, public-policy and public-security conditions in the applicable framework.
This is not a rule for a refugee, residence, or other non-national travel document issued by one of these states.

policies.title: British citizens: Common Travel Area entry
policies.summary: A British citizen using an ordinary British passport does not need an Irish visa; British and Irish citizens have Common Travel Area travel rights.
conditions: This normalizes the catalog's United Kingdom ordinary passport as a British-citizen case, not every possible British-status document.

The Common Travel Area guidance says an officer makes no further requirement when satisfied of CTA citizenship and travel from the United Kingdom; carry evidence of identity, nationality and route if requested.
The official nationality table separately distinguishes British protected persons and named British-status documents; those document categories are not flattened into this policy.

policies.title: Listed non-EEA ordinary passports: no Irish visa required
policies.summary: The listed nationalities are marked 'No' in Immigration Service Delivery's current visa-nationality table, so an ordinary national passport holder does not need an Irish visa before a short visit.
conditions: Applies only to the ordinary national-passport nationality row. It does not cover a Hong Kong Document of Identity, refugee or stateless document, diplomatic, official, service, British-status, or other special travel document.
No pre-travel visa does not itself authorise landing or residence: an immigration officer makes the permission decision and may attach duration and activity conditions.
The official nationality table does not state one universal visitor duration for this cohort; do not infer one from the visa-waiver classification.
Ukraine is included because the current nationality table marks it as not visa-required; it also appears in the UK-waiver programme but does not need that conditional programme to be visa-free.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Irish short-stay visa required
policies.summary: The listed nationalities are marked 'Yes' in Immigration Service Delivery's current table and therefore require an Irish visa before ordinary short-stay visitor travel, unless a separately stated status-, document-, school-group-, UK-visa-, BIVS-, or other legal exception is met.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports only; it does not classify special British, refugee, stateless, diplomatic, official, service, United Nations, or other travel documents.
For a tourism visit of 90 days or less, use the Short Stay (C) visitor route; an issued visa permits travel but does not guarantee entry or a particular landing-stamp duration.
This policy is the ordinary case. The status/document exemptions, Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme and BIVS policies below are narrow alternatives, not universal eVisa or ETA eligibility.
Nicaragua, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia have been visa-required since 15 June 2026; the 2026 order also added them to the transit-visa schedule.

application.label: Official AVATS Irish visa application service
application.processingTime: Immigration Service Delivery says generally about 8 weeks after it receives documents; timing can vary by office and case.
steps: Confirm that no document-, residence-status, UK-visa, BIVS, or other limited exception applies and select the visitor purpose that matches the trip.
Create the application in AVATS, selecting Short Stay (C), Visit Tourist, and the appropriate single or multiple journey type.
Pay the required fee where applicable, then submit the signed AVATS summary, passport and supporting documents to the office AVATS identifies.

policies.title: Visa-required nationalities: Irish-residence and EU-family-card document exemptions
policies.summary: A visa-required ordinary-passport holder can travel without a separate Irish visa when holding one of the specific Irish-residence, Irish-issued travel-document, or Article 10 EU-family-member documents identified by Immigration Service Delivery.
conditions: The traveller must hold a valid Irish Residence Permit, an Irish-issued travel document, or a 'Residence card of a family member of a Union citizen' issued under Article 10 of Directive 2004/38/EC by any country.
This is a document/status-specific exception; it does not make the named nationalities generally visa-free and does not establish that a different residence card qualifies.
The Irish guidance directs holders to the issuing authority for advice on whether a purported family-member card falls within the Directive as implemented by that state.
The page separately addresses 1951 and 1954 Convention documents and temporary refugee arrangements; those special travel-document rules are not normalized as ordinary-passport nationality access.

policies.title: Eligible visa-required nationalities: conditional UK Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme
policies.summary: The listed passport holders may visit Ireland without a separate Irish visa only through the Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, with an eligible UK short-stay visa and every stated UK-entry, passport, purpose and remaining-leave condition met.
conditions: This programme is only for the listed passport issuers with an eligible UK short-stay visitor visa; a UK ETA alone cannot be used for this programme.

The traveller must first have landed and gained lawful entry to the UK using the current UK visa, except where the official page's already-used-UK rule applies; UK visitor-in-transit and marriage/civil-partnership visas are excluded.
The Irish visit must end before UK leave expires and is limited to 90 days or the remaining UK permission, whichever is shorter; Irish entry remains a border decision.

For BH, KW, OM, QA, SA and PE, only a qualifying UK short-stay visa issued before the relevant UK ETA introduction can be used. Ukraine is already generally visa-free under the current Irish nationality table.

policies.title: Chinese and Indian passports: conditional British-Irish Visa Scheme route
policies.summary: Chinese and Indian nationals can use a single BIVS-endorsed eligible Irish or UK short-stay visa for Ireland and the United Kingdom when their residence, visa endorsement, purpose, first-entry and duration conditions are met.
conditions: CN applies only to Chinese nationals living in China, including Hong Kong or Macao, at application; IN applies only to Indian nationals living in India at application.
The visa must be endorsed 'BIVS'; endorsement is considered by the visa officer and is not guaranteed.
A holder of a UK-issued BIVS visa must enter the UK first before Ireland; eligible UK visitor categories exclude visitor in transit and visitor for marriage or civil partnership.
It is for short visits only, up to 90 days or the end of UK permission if shorter, and does not guarantee Irish entry. This does not change the normal visa-required classification for CN or IN.

policies.title: Named nationalities: airport/seaport transit visa requirement
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require an Irish transit visa to pass through an Irish airport or seaport to another state. This is a transit-only rule and does not create a different ordinary visitor-entry status.
conditions: Applies only to transit through an Irish airport or seaport en route to another state; it is not an ordinary short-stay visitor-visa determination.

A connection that requires border control, including leaving a terminal, collecting bags, changing terminals in some cases, or overnight transit, instead requires the appropriate Irish entry permission and entry visa where applicable.
A transit visa can be used for a same-day Dublin Terminal 2 connection only when both flights are between 04:00 and 20:00; all passengers present to an immigration officer.

Ethiopia has a narrow no-transit-visa exception for direct Ethiopia–Ireland–United States/Canada travel on a national passport with destination permission, and lawful return travel from the United States or Canada.

application.label: Official AVATS Irish transit-visa application service
application.processingTime: Immigration Service Delivery says generally about 8 weeks after it receives transit-visa documents.
steps: Confirm that the journey is transit rather than entry and that no narrow Ethiopia transit exception applies.
Create an AVATS application, selecting Transit and the appropriate single or multiple journey type.
Pay the fee where applicable and submit the AVATS summary, passport, itinerary, onward-permission evidence and requested documents to the identified office.

policies.title: Ethiopian national passports: narrow direct United States or Canada transit exception
policies.summary: An Ethiopian citizen on a national passport does not need an Irish transit visa for the specified direct Ethiopia–Ireland–United States/Canada or return journey, subject to destination-permission and lawful-presence conditions. This is not visitor visa-free access.
conditions: Only for direct travel from Ethiopia via Ireland to the United States or Canada with permission to travel to that destination, or direct return from the United States or Canada to Ethiopia via Ireland after lawful presence there.
Only waives the Irish transit visa; it does not waive the ordinary Irish visitor visa requirement or guarantee permission to enter Ireland.
If transit circumstances require border control, the traveller must meet the appropriate Irish entry requirements.
